edition.notes: Swete prints the ancient anonymous Latin translation with Greek fragments and an extensive introduction. The Latin witnesses had circulated under Ambrose or Hilary; Swete argues from their contents and agreements with extant Greek fragments that the work is Theodore's. No surviving Greek fragment printed here independently preserves the exact Galatians 3:19 identification of the mediator as Moses.
edition.publication: Edited by H. B. Swete, Cambridge: University Press, 1880
edition.title: Theodori Episcopi Mopsuesteni in Epistolas B. Pauli Commentarii: The Latin Version with the Greek Fragments, Volume I: Introduction; Galatians-Colossians

passages.context: On Galatians 3:19-20, the ancient Latin version of Theodore's commentary says that the Law was added because of transgressions, was ministered by angels, and names Moses as the referent of 'in the hand of a mediator.' It explains Moses's mediation between God and the people and insists that the same one God gave the Law and manifested the more excellent realities belonging to Christ.
passages.notes: Read directly at printed pp. 47-49, artifact PDF pp. 146-148; the decisive sentence appears on printed p. 48: 'quod dixit: in manu mediatoris, Moysi dicit.' This supports the narrow claim that Theodore's transmitted commentary identifies the mediator here as Moses. Because no Greek fragment at this exact point survives in Swete, cite it as the ancient Latin version's witness to Theodore's sense, not as an exact reconstruction of Theodore's Greek wording or a denial of Christ's mediation in other senses.
